catalog_quote: Stress placement in Roma is predominantly penultimate, with a secondary stress (indicated by ˌ in the relevant examples) on the pre-antepenultimate syllable if there is one (Steven 1991:42ff): (2) 'pi.ti 'mat' 'wo.ha 'paddle' da'mu.lan 'bamboo (species)' er'we.run 'gall, bile' Morphemes four syllables in length are rare in Roma, with only two known forms (both nouns) as possible candidates: (3) ˌdil.kor'kor.ra 'frog' ˌko.kam'ma.u 'spider' Morphologically complex forms are not unusual, however, and they also show secondary stress ...: (4) ˌi.tam.'tur.wi.ti 'we (incl) sleep/rest' ˌa.mal'we.ra.mi 'we (excl) bathe' ... The examples in (4) illustrate a major exception to the pattern of penultimate stress which is important, viz. that suffixes are not considered when stress placement is assigned. ... (5) klodan 'klo.dan 'shin' klodan+na 'klo.dan.na 'his shin' aw+mturu+au am'tur.wa.u 'I sleep' na+mturu+e nam'tur.we 'he sleeps' ama+mturu+ami ˌa.mam'tur.wa.mi 'we (excl) sleep' ita+mturu+iti ˌi.tam'tur.wi.ti 'we (incl) sleep' [p. 87] This pattern must be distinguished from that resulting from the attachment of other affixal material (referred to here as 'clitics'), which do cause the stress to shift (Steven 1991:45): (6) lepa 'le.pa 'monkey' lepa+ei le'pei 'the monkey' lepa+ida le'pida 'a monkey' krahan 'kra.han 'house' krahan+ei kra.ha'ne.i 'the house' krahan+ida kra.ha'ni.da 'a house'

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the stem/root (ˈpi.ti, daˈmu.lan). Suffixes are invisible to stress assignment, so stress stays on the stem's penult even when suffixes follow (ˈklo.dan.na 'his shin', amˈtur.wa.u 'I sleep'); enclitics such as =ei 'the' and =ida 'a' do count, and stress moves to the penult of the whole form (leˈpei, kra.haˈne.i). Longer forms carry a secondary stress on the pre-antepenultimate syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the pre-antepenultimate syllable when the form has one: ˌdil.korˈkor.ra 'frog', ˌko.kamˈma.u 'spider', ˌi.tamˈtur.wi.ti 'we (incl) sleep', ˌa.mamˈtur.wa.mi 'we (excl) sleep'.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged as 'predominantly' penultimate. Stated exception: suffixes are not counted (stress on stem penult, i.e. antepenult or earlier of the surface word: ˈklo.dan.na, amˈtur.wa.u, nam.ˈtur.we), whereas enclitics =ei/=ida shift stress to the surface penult (leˈpei, leˈpida, kra.haˈne.i, kra.haˈni.da). Four-syllable morphemes are rare (two known nouns).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word including affixes; citation forms). The statement is a summary by the thesis author (Steven) with his UTA advisor; the full treatment is Steven 1991: 42ff (stress) and 45 (clitic vs suffix). Intonation is covered in the thesis but not in this paper.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes Roma as spoken on Roma (Romang) island, southern Maluku (Burquest & Steven 1994:85), from Steven's 1991 field data; matches roma1332 / ISO rmm. No dialect is named; Wikipedia (from Ethnologue) locates it at Jersusu village. Not to be confused with Romani.
